instruction:
Fix `packages/excalidraw/tests/textStyleRanges.test.tsx` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. Senior review findings on this test file (keep every existing test passing; no snapshots; no `toEqual([])` for styleRanges):
1 (major) Add a test: open the editor on 'hello world', colour 6..11, then setSelectionRange(0, 11) + fireEvent.select and run actionChangeStrokeColor {color:'#1971c2'}. Expect strokeColor '#1971c2' and the element to have no styleRanges key (or no range with `color`). The source now does this: a whole-text selection takes the element-wide path and clears every range's `color` (actionProperties.tsx).
2 (minor) Add a test that selects 6..11 and runs fireEvent.click(screen.getByTestId('text-highlight-#ffec99')) (check the real test id in components/TextHighlightPicker.tsx), then asserts styleRanges has a range 6..11 with that backgroundColor.
3 (minor) Replace `as any` reads of results with `isTextElement` narrowing (keep `as any` only for deliberately invalid restore input). Move the repeated open-editor-and-select sequence into a local `openEditorWithSelection(text, start, end)` helper.
A previous attempt failed only because staticSvgScene.ts was broken at the time (0 <text> nodes); that is fixed now and the current file passes all 16 tests.

The file's current text is under Inputs, marked "current text"; your edits apply to exactly that text.

## Answer
Return ONLY a JSON object {"path": "packages/excalidraw/tests/textStyleRanges.test.tsx", "edits": [{"search": "<text copied exactly from the current text>", "replace": "<its replacement>"}]} with no other text. Each search must appear exactly once in the current text; the edits apply in order.
If the file does not exist yet, or the change rewrites most of it, return {"path": "packages/excalidraw/tests/textStyleRanges.test.tsx", "content": "<the complete file>"} instead.
